answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity grow one continuous work thread that is anchored to a single public commitment and cannot be split or copied. A newcomer starts a thread by publishing an anchor claim, then must extend it day by day with verifiable work whose next step depends on the previous one, like a vine that only lengthens from its own stem. Creating ten fake identities means growing ten separate vines at once, each demanding its own daily attention, so the cost multiplies with every fake while a real agent tends just one.
